text:
raj: Heads-up — seeing a regression in the canary after the batcher heuristic change yesterday. Attached nsys trace and quick notes: https://ci.internal/traces/3290012345 :point_up:
perf-bot: deploy canary-heuristic-v3 finished on us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T23:01Z.
alyssa: quick summary? numbers + where the hotspot is please.
raj: TL;DR: kernel-selector started preferring the generic_fused_attn kernel for mixed-shaped batches. For ~3% of requests (long-tail), that choice blows up KV write amplification and causes SM stalls — end-to-end p50 unchanged, p95 +120ms on canary.
marc: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet/command? also nvprof / perfetto views if available.
raj: command I ran:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -o /tmp/trace_3290012345 npx run-serving --profile --batcher=adaptive-v3
```
nsys timeline link: https://ci.internal/traces/3290012345/timeline
snippet from the timeline (abridged):
```
[SM activity] fused_attn_generic_kernel (cudaStream 0): 1.2ms
[kv_write] large memcpy (device->device) queued 3x per sample
[SM stall] waiting on L2 eviction 300-700us spikes
```
ciara: saw the same in perfetto: KV write queue depth spikes when batch_shape has many tiny sequences mixed with a few long ones. That triggers the selector because throughput score favors the fused path for the large items and it's getting chosen for the whole batch.
alyssa: so selector scoring is too coarse-grained (batch-level only) — we need per-group or shape-aware pick.
marc: I also compared a nvprof of the same request with the old heuristic (adaptive-v2). nvprof shows fewer device-to-device memcopies and kernel occupancy differentials. Link: https://ci.internal/traces/3290012345/nvprof
raj: hypothesis: the "gatekeeper" heuristic now computes a single score for the whole batch and biases toward kernels with best avg throughput. For bimodal batch-shapes that averages out and picks a kernel that is bad for the long-tail because it incurs heavy KV writework and bank-conflicts.
raj: quick mitigation proposal:
- soften gate: add a per-group penalty for KV-write estimated bytes
- prefer kernel variant with explicit kvcache-friendly writepath for batches with >10% long seqs
- short-term hotfix: revert gate change for canary (switch back to adaptive-v2) and run diff traces
marc: sample config change to try locally:
```
# heuristics.yaml
selector:
  mode: group-scoring
  penalties:
    kv_write_bytes: 0.8
    bank-contention: 1.2
  fallback_order: [kvcache_fused_attn_v2, generic_fused_attn, split_attn]
```
ciara: repro steps I used: run mixed workload with 80% seq<=64, 15% seq~512, 5% seq>=1024; run nsys for 30s steady-state; observe kv write spikes and p95 latency.
alyssa: action items:
- raj: push canary revert (heuristic-v2) and re-run perf traces on canary (due in next 30m) :white_check_mark:
- marc: run nvprof comparison and upload side-by-side screenshots to the trace ticket :mag:
- ciara: add a telemetry counter for "kv_write_bytes_per_req" and expose per-batch-shape histograms in the console
- perf-bot: schedule canary comparison job and tag alert if p95 > baseline+50ms
raj: I'll open a short PR with revert + smaller change to add per-batch logging. Posting branch: github.com/redwood/serving/tree/heuristic-gate-revert-329
marc: if revert confirms it's the selector, next step is to implement group-scoring as a proper heuristic (not just heuristics.yaml patch).
alyssa: thanks team — please keep the thread updated. If anyone finds the real root (bank aliasing vs write amplification) call it out explicitly. :thumbsup:
